summary: AI-powered web scraping and browser automation has shifted from raw HTML parsing toward LLM-native pipelines that return clean, structured, agent-ready data. Modern tools emphasize natural-language extraction, MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration for AI agents like Claude and Cursor, and managed cloud browser infrastructure that handles JavaScript rendering, stealth, and session persistence. The market is growing rapidly, with the AI browser segment projected to expand from $4.5B in 2024 to $76.8B by 2034, and roughly 79% of companies already adopting some form of AI agent technology.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open source (self-hosted); costs only arise from hosting/compute
ai_features: AI-assisted codegen and test generation
Integrates with LLM agents for navigation and extraction
MCP server available for agent-driven browser control
strengths: Robust handling of dynamic, JavaScript-heavy pages
Huge community and extensive language bindings
tools.best_for: Developers needing full, reliable browser automation for dynamic pages with clicks, form fills, and extraction

tools.name: Puppeteer
ai_features: Pairs with LLM pipelines for automated extraction
Used as the browser layer under many AI agent frameworks
strengths: Lightweight and fast for Node.js workflows
tools.best_for: Node.js developers automating Chromium for scraping and headless browser tasks

tools.name: Scrapy
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open source; Zyte Cloud plans start around $25/mo
ai_features: Integrates with LLM extraction middleware
Works alongside AI parsers for structured output
strengths: Python default for medium-to-large scale scraping
tools.best_for: Python developers building large-scale, static-content crawlers

tools.name: Selenium
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open source; grid hosting via third parties varies
ai_features: Integrates with AI testing and self-healing locator tools
Used as browser layer for AI automation agents
strengths: Supports virtually all languages and browsers
tools.best_for: Teams needing broad language/browser support for web automation and testing

tools.name: Beautiful Soup
ai_features: Commonly paired with LLMs to parse and structure extracted HTML
tools.best_for: Quick, small-to-medium static HTML parsing in Python

tools.name: Firecrawl
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier with limited credits; paid plans start around $19/mo scaling with credits
ai_features: LLM-ready clean markdown output
Natural-language structured extraction
Handles JavaScript, crawling, and browser interaction in one API
strengths: AI-native output optimized for LLM pipelines
Single API for search, scrape, and browser interaction
Fast setup and integration for agents
tools.best_for: Developers building AI agents or LLM pipelines needing clean, ready-to-use web data

tools.name: Apify
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier with $5 monthly credits; paid plans start at $49/mo
ai_features: MCP integration for AI agents
AI-ready data output and LLM-oriented actors
Marketplace of pre-built scrapers
strengths: Flexible for complex, configurable scraping jobs
tools.best_for: Teams wanting pre-built scrapers or a general-purpose automation platform

tools.name: Browserbase
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier for testing; paid plans start around $20/mo scaling with browser hours

Stealth proxies and session persistence for agent workflows
Supports AI frameworks via Playwright/Puppeteer

tools.name: AgentQL
